# QP balanced broad sector: rank-two prime chart and divided-secants gate

**Date:** 2026-08-23  
**Verdict:** fixing the rational plane generated by the first two reduced
lattice directions gives an exact rank-two analogue of the prime-power
common-parameter chart.  If

```text
P=lambda1*lambda2,
```

then one fixed plane contains at most

```text
M*(1+q/P)                                           (0.1)
```

actual color vectors from a coefficient support of size `M`.  On a flat
bin its weighted color mass is therefore

```text
(1+q/P)/M.                                         (0.2)
```

At the balanced broad survivor

```text
lambda1~lambda2~lambda3~D^(11/16),
P=D^(22/16),       K=D/lambda3=D^(5/16),
q=D^(33/16),       M=D^(15/8),                     (0.3)
```

(0.1) is `D^(41/16)` and (0.2) is `D^(-19/16)`.
This is a strong fixed-plane theorem, but the plane varies with the color.
Even the optimistic saturated-fiber ledger permits `D^2` plane labels,
whereas a direct union argument would need at most `M=D^(15/8)` labels.
The mismatch is exactly `D^(1/8)`.

There is an additional exact structural reduction.  For points selected
from ordered occupied slices, suitable divided second differences lie in
the first-two-directions plane.  Two independent such differences recover
that plane, and together with one transverse secant recover the primitive
color normal.  If all the divided second differences are collinear, the
selected points lie in one affine two-plane.  Its determinant section is a
binary affine conic; in the nonparabolic broad sector it has only `q^o(1)`
integral points.  Thus a power-sized nonparabolic chain necessarily contains
a four-endpoint configuration which recovers its plane.

What is not proved is a weighted bounded-overlap theorem for those varying
four-point plane labels.  The existing fixed-secant and two-fixed-relation
partial matchings apply after the labels are fixed, but their raw union is
not bounded by `D`.  Consequently this note gives a precise reduction of
the balanced broad endpoint, not the sharp four-cycle theorem.

---

## 1. Exact third-slice normal form

For an oriented all-distinct color matrix put

```text
w_C=(c11,-c12,-c21,c22),
Lambda_C={E in Z^4 : w_C dot E=0}.                 (1.1)
```

Distinct actual prime powers in the project shell are pairwise coprime, so
`w_C` is primitive.  Choose a reduced integral basis

```text
V1,V2,V3 of Lambda_C,
||Vi||~lambdai,       lambda1<=lambda2<=lambda3.   (1.2)
```

Fix one completion product matrix `P0`.  Every other completion has the
form

```text
P(x,y,t)=P0+x*V1+y*V2+t*V3,                        (1.3)
```

with

```text
|x|<<D/lambda1, |y|<<D/lambda2, |t|<<D/lambda3.   (1.4)
```

The completion condition is `det P=0`.  On one third slice it is

```text
F_t(x,y)=a*x^2+b*x*y+c*y^2+d(t)*x+e(t)*y+f(t)=0.  (1.5)
```

The coefficients `a,b,c` do not depend on `t`.  In the nondegenerate broad
case

```text
Delta=b^2-4*a*c !=0.                               (1.6)
```

For example, when `a!=0`, put

```text
X=2*a*x+b*y+d(t),
g=b*d(t)-2*a*e(t),
h=d(t)^2-4*a*f(t),
Y=Delta*y+g.                                       (1.7)
```

On (1.5) these obey the exact binary norm equation

```text
Y^2-Delta*X^2=g^2-Delta*h.                         (1.8)
```

The cases `a=0` are obtained by interchanging variables or by a linear
completion.  A nonzero right side has `q^o(1)` integral solutions in a
polynomial-size box.  A zero or singular right side is a union of at most
two rational lines; actual pair uniqueness and the fact that every nonzero
same-color secant is invertible leave `O(1)` completions.  Hence one fixed
nondegenerate slice costs `q^o(1)`.

At (0.3), all three coordinate ranges in (1.4) have length `K=D^(5/16)`.
The unresolved factor is the number of occupied `t` values, not the number
of points on one slice.

## 2. The orthogonal rank-two lattice

Let

```text
W=span_Q(V1,V2),
Gamma_W=W^perp intersect Z^4.                      (2.1)
```

Write `B` for the `2 by 4` integral matrix whose rows are `V1,V2`.
Because `V1,V2` are part of a basis of the primitive lattice `Lambda_C`,
`Z*V1+Z*V2` is saturated in `Z^4`.  Equivalently,

```text
gcd of the six 2 by 2 minors of B is 1.            (2.2)
```

The same fact follows from

```text
*(V1 wedge V2 wedge V3)=+-w_C                     (2.3)
```

and the primitivity of `w_C`.

Choose a coordinate pair `I` for which

```text
Delta_I=|det B_I|
```

is maximal, and let `J` be its complementary pair.  Reducedness gives

```text
Delta_I~||V1 wedge V2||~lambda1*lambda2=P.         (2.4)
```

### Lemma 2.1 (exact complementary projection index)

The projection onto the coordinates in `J` is injective on `Gamma_W`, and
its image is a sublattice of `Z^2` of index exactly `Delta_I`.

**Proof.**  Write `B=[B_I|B_J]`.  A vector `(x,y)` with the `I|J`
coordinate split belongs to `Gamma_W` exactly when

```text
B_I*x=-B_J*y.                                      (2.5)
```

Since `B_I` is nonsingular, `y` determines `x`; this proves injectivity.
The image is

```text
L={y in Z^2 : B_J*y belongs to B_I*Z^2}.           (2.6)
```

Condition (2.2) says that the four columns of `B` generate `Z^2`.  Hence
the two columns of `B_J` generate `Z^2/B_I Z^2`, and the map

```text
Z^2 -> Z^2/B_I Z^2,       y |-> B_J*y             (2.7)
```

is onto.  Its kernel is `L`, so

```text
[Z^2:L]=|det B_I|=Delta_I.                         (2.8)
```

## 3. Prime powers in an index-`Delta` planar lattice

Let `A` be a subset of the actual prime powers in the project shell and
write `|A|=M`.  The ratio of the largest shell point to the smallest is
strictly less than two.

### Lemma 3.1 (rank-two prime chart)

For every index-`Delta` sublattice `L` of `Z^2`,

```text
#(L intersect (A times A)) << M*(1+q/Delta).       (3.1)
```

**Proof.**  Let the first-coordinate projection of `L` be `h Z`, and let
its vertical kernel be `(0,m Z)`.  Hermite normal form gives

```text
h*m=Delta.                                         (3.2)
```

If `h>1`, every first coordinate is divisible by `h`.  An actual prime
power divisible by `h` must have the unique prime base dividing `h` (or no
such point exists), and the ratio-`<2` shell contains at most one power of
that base.  There are then at most `M` pairs.

If `h=1`, then `m=Delta`.  For each fixed first coordinate, the second
coordinate lies in one residue class modulo `Delta`, giving
`O(1+q/Delta)` choices in the shell.  This proves (3.1).  Signs change only
an absolute constant.

Apply the lemma to the image in Lemma 2.1.  Projection is injective, so one
fixed rational plane `W` supports at most

```text
M*(1+q/P)                                          (3.3)
```

actual color normals.  If a flat bin has squared mass `Z^2`, then every
color weight is `O(Z^4/M^2)`, and therefore

```text
sum_(C: W(C)=W) w_z(C)
 <<(1+q/P)*M^(-1)*q^o(1)*Z^4.                     (3.4)
```

## 4. The exact balanced ledger

At (0.3),

```text
q/P=D^(11/16),
# colors per fixed W <=D^(30/16+11/16)=D^(41/16),
fixed-W flat mass <=D^(41/16-60/16)=D^(-19/16).   (4.1)
```

The principal determinant-band count at this support size is

```text
N_col=M^3*D/q=D^(90/16+16/16-33/16)=D^(73/16).   (4.2)
```

The desired occupied-slice estimate is

```text
sum_C J(C) <=D*M^2=D^(76/16),                     (4.3)
```

whereas the pointwise slice cap gives only

```text
K*N_col=D^(5/16+73/16)=D^(78/16).                 (4.4)
```

Even if every fixed-plane fiber in (4.1) were saturated, (4.2) could be
distributed among

```text
N_col / D^(41/16)=D^2                             (4.5)
```

plane labels.  A direct sum of (3.3) followed by the factor `K` would need
at most

```text
(D*M^2)/(K*D^(41/16))=D^(30/16)=M                 (4.6)
```

labels.  Equations (4.5)--(4.6) differ by `D^(2/16)=D^(1/8)`.  No current
theorem bounds the number, energy, or weighted overlap of the canonical
planes at the scale (4.6).  Notice also that when all three minima are
comparable, the designation of the first two basis vectors is not an
intrinsic physical slicing; a deterministic reduction convention makes it
well-defined but does not create orthogonality across colors.

## 5. Divided second differences remove the local basis ambiguity

Choose one completion point `P_i` in each of a sequence of ordered occupied
slices

```text
t_0<t_1<...<t_s.
```

Put

```text
h_i=t_(i+1)-t_i,
E_i=P_(i+1)-P_i.                                   (5.1)
```

Writing `P_i=P0+t_i*V3+w_i` with `w_i in W` gives

```text
E_i=h_i*V3+(w_(i+1)-w_i).                          (5.2)
```

Consequently the integral divided-second-difference numerator

```text
F_i=h_(i+1)*E_i-h_i*E_(i+1)                       (5.3)
```

lies exactly in `W`.  Also, for any two occupied endpoints with slice gap
`h`,

```text
*(V1 wedge V2 wedge E)=+-h*w_C.                   (5.4)
```

If two `F_i,F_j` are independent, then

```text
W=span_Q(F_i,F_j),
Q*Lambda_C=W direct-sum Q*E_k,                    (5.5)
```

for any nonzero slice secant `E_k`.  In particular the primitive color
normal is recovered by

```text
w_C=primitive(*(F_i wedge F_j wedge E_k)),         (5.6)
```

with its orientation fixed by the color sign pattern.  When
`F_i,F_(i+1)` are independent, four consecutive selected endpoints suffice.

There is also a direct four-endpoint formulation which does not require
consecutive occupied slices.  Given four selected points with distinct
indices `t_0,t_1,t_2,t_3`, put `E_j=P_j-P_0` and

```text
G_j=(t_1-t_0)*E_j-(t_j-t_0)*E_1,       j=2,3.     (5.6a)
```

Both `G_2,G_3` lie in `W`.  They are independent exactly when
`P_0,P_1,P_2,P_3` are affinely independent, because the spans of
`E_1,E_2,E_3` and `E_1,G_2,G_3` coincide.  In that event (5.5)--(5.6),
with `G_2,G_3`, recover `W` and `w_C` from those four physical endpoints.

There is no unspecified proportionality factor in this recovery.  Write

```text
E_j=sum_i n_(i,j)*V_i,             H=det(n_(i,j)).
```

Then multilinearity and (2.3) give

```text
*(E_1 wedge E_2 wedge E_3)=+-H*w_C.               (5.6b)
```

Thus every signed `3 by 3` endpoint minor is exactly `H` times the
corresponding actual color, and division by the common content recovers the
primitive `w_C`.  At the balanced point `|n_(i,j)|<<K`, so `|H|<<K^3`;
if the four slice indices have bounded diameter, expansion along their
third-coordinate row improves this to `|H|<<K^2`.  This exact divisibility
is a possible arithmetic input for the remaining endpoint-union problem,
but no summed divisor estimate strong enough for (6.2) is currently proved.

### Lemma 5.1 (collinear divided differences force a plane conic)

Suppose all the nonzero `F_i` lie in one rational line `Q ell` in `W`.
Then all selected points lie in one affine rational two-plane.

**Proof.**  In `Q^4/Q ell`, (5.3) says

```text
E_i/h_i=E_(i+1)/h_(i+1).                           (5.7)
```

Thus all divided slopes agree modulo `ell`.  For one lift `v` of their
common class,

```text
P_i=P_0+(t_i-t_0)*v+a_i*ell                       (5.8)
```

for rational `a_i`.  This is the asserted affine plane.

On that plane, `det P=0` becomes one binary affine quadratic in `(t,a)`.
If its quadratic discriminant is nonzero, the completion-of-squares
argument in Section 1 gives `q^o(1)` integral points.  If it is singular or
reducible, its line components contain at most one actual point each,
because a difference along such a component has determinant zero.  If the
restriction vanishes identically, the line through any two of its points
also lies in the determinant quadric, so their secant has determinant zero;
again there is at most one actual point.  Hence a power-sized collinear
chain can occur only when the
quadratic part has zero discriminant but the affine equation remains
irreducible: precisely the parabolic/tangent plane-section branch.

Therefore, in the balanced **nonparabolic** broad sector, every
power-sized occupied chain contains independent divided second differences
and admits the intrinsic reconstruction (5.5)--(5.6).

Equivalently, if no four endpoints give the reconstruction (5.6a), the
whole selected set has affine dimension at most two and is already in the
plane-conic alternative of Lemma 5.1.  This is the basis-free local
dichotomy; it does not by itself count the varying four-endpoint labels.

## 6. What the reconstruction does and does not prove

After `F_i,F_j` are fixed, the two-relation partial-matching theorem gives

```text
sum_(C: w_C dot F_i=w_C dot F_j=0) w_z(C)
 <<q^o(1)*||z||_2^4.                               (6.1)
```

This is compatible with the fixed-plane estimate (3.4).  However, the
vectors in (5.3) vary with the four completion endpoints.  Product-window
shortness gives only `||E_i||<<D` and, for bounded slice gaps,
`||F_i||<<D*q^o(1)`; it does not give `O(D)` possible independent pairs.
The existing fixed-secant theorem similarly applies only after `E_k` is
fixed.  Summing either (6.1) or the fixed-secant estimate over all realized
labels recreates the unresolved secant/plane energy.

The exact missing statement is the occupied-slice incidence bound below;
a sufficient fixed-plane formulation is the accompanying effective-label
bound:

```text
weighted occupied-slice incidence <=D*M^2,         (6.2)

or

effective number/energy of high-J plane labels
    <=M*q^o(1),                                    (6.3)
```

where (6.3) must be interpreted with the fiber weights in (3.3), not as a
raw count of all rational planes.  Current fixed-label theorems do not imply
(6.3).

For comparison, the ternary cone

```text
x*y=t^2                                            (6.4)
```

has `K^(1-o(1))` occupied `t` values in a `K` box while each fixed slice is
a divisor conic.  Taking points

```text
(x,y,t)=(u^2,v^2,u*v)                              (6.5)
```

with `u,v` primes in disjoint intervals of length comparable with
`sqrt(K)` gives `K/log(K)^2` distinct slices and pairwise non-null secants.
This is a valid determinant-quadric warning against using only the
per-slice norm-equation bound.  It is not a counterexample to Lemma 5.1:
the points in (6.5) range through the full ternary cone, rather than one
affine two-plane, so their divided second differences recover varying
two-planes.  It is also not an actual prime-power QP counterexample.

```text
fixed-W rank-two prime chart:                       PROVED;
balanced fixed-plane exponent D^(-19/16):           PROVED;
divided-second-difference reconstruction:           PROVED;
collinear nonparabolic chain q^o(1):                PROVED;
weighted union over varying reconstructed planes:   OPEN;
balanced broad D^(1/8) saving and sharp FC:          OPEN.
```
